story_title: As an authorised Event Coordinator, I want to update permitted event information so that event details remain accurate during planning

acceptance_criteria.text: Authorised users can update permitted event information.
Changes are reflected in the event record.
Users cannot edit information they are not authorised to modify.
Important information such as date, time, attendance, venue and equipment requirements is identified as affecting existing arrangements.

Given important information is changed on an event with existing venue, equipment or registration arrangements, when the change is saved, then the affected arrangements are identified and flagged for review rather than automatically changed.

Given the event is Confirmed and the change affects its essential arrangements, when the change is saved, then the event status reverts (e.g. to Planning) so it can be reconfirmed. Notifying the Event Organiser that it is no longer confirmed is covered by Receive Event Notifications (SPM-53).
An ordinary edit that does not affect existing arrangements does not flag arrangements or change the event status.

test_cases.preconditions:
Test data loaded: `npm run fixtures:spm62` has been run from the project folder since the last full `npx prisma db seed` (it only touches the 'SPM62 …' events, never anyone else's data).
Logged in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), the coordinator assigned to every 'SPM62 …' event.
Nothing is saved in this case.
steps: Click 'All Events' in the sidebar and open 'SPM62 Harbour Leadership Summit'
test_cases.test_data: Event: SPM62 Harbour Leadership Summit | Status: Planning | When: 17 Mar 2027, 09:00–17:00 | Expected attendance: 80 | Layout: Theatre | Required facility: Fixed ceiling projector
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 1: The event page shows the 'Planning' status badge and an 'Edit event information' button at the top of the page.
Step 2: The 'Edit event information' page opens with the 'Planning' status badge. The form is filled in with the event's current information: Event name 'SPM62 Harbour Leadership Summit', Starts at 17 Mar 2027 09:00, Ends at 17 Mar 2027 17:00, Expected attendance 80, Preferred room layout 'Theatre', and 'Fixed ceiling projector' ticked under 'The venue must have'. There are no fields for Organiser, Company, Coordinator or Status, no Registration section, and no equipment rows: an info message reads 'Equipment is changed on the Equipment tab.' The buttons are 'Save changes' and 'Cancel'. No amber warning is shown.
Step 3: The event page opens again with the 'Planning' status badge and the same details as in step 1.

Step 3: No amber warning appears. A description change does not affect arrangements.

Step 8: The event page opens with nothing changed: 'When' in the Details card shows '17 Mar 2027, 09:00–17:00' and 'Expected attendance' shows '80'. No 'Event information updated.' alert is shown.

open_questions: Written before the code (TDD, 2026-10-05). Every label, message, page address and rule below marked DECIDED was chosen here, in the style of the existing screens, and is what the developer now builds to. Change any of them before the code is written and update the cases with it.

DECIDED 2026-10-05: who may edit (AC1, AC3). Only the coordinator assigned to the event. The organiser who raised it (after submission changes go through the coordinator, clarification #102), other coordinators, the Ops Manager, Venue Staff, Technical Support and Attendees may not.

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: when (AC3). Only while the event is Approved, Planning or Confirmed. Under review is the request still being decided (SPM-28); Completed, Cancelled, Rejected and Withdrawn are final. Postponed is not editable in this story: rescheduling a postponed event goes through resuming it (Postponed -> Approved) first.

DECIDED 2026-10-05: the page is 'Edit event information' at /events/<reference>/update, reached from an 'Edit event information' button at the top of the event page (shown only to the assigned coordinator in those statuses). The organiser's draft editor at /events/<reference>/edit is unchanged. After saving, the form is replaced on the same page by a green alert 'Event information updated.' ('Event information updated. The event is back in Planning and needs to be confirmed again.' when the status reverted), what the save flagged (see 'who sees the flags'), and a 'Back to event' link. Refusal: red alert 'You can't edit this event's information' with 'Only the coordinator assigned to this event can change its information.' or 'Event information can only be changed while the event is Approved, Planning or Confirmed.', and a 'Back to event' button.

DECIDED 2026-10-05: the permitted fields (AC1, AC3) are the organiser's request fields, with the same labels and validation messages as the draft form (S-08): Event name, Type of event, Purpose, Description, Starts at, Ends at, Expected attendance, Preferred room layout, The venue must have, Accessibility needs, Other accessibility notes and Anything else about the space. Not on the form: organiser, company, coordinator, status and reference; equipment, which is changed on the Equipment tab (SPM-47; the form says 'Equipment is changed on the Equipment tab.'); and the registration settings, which are Configure Event Registration's (SPM-64, see below).

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: multi-session events. Their per-session times, attendance and layout are shown read-only here ('Session times and attendance can't be changed here yet.'). Editing sessions is a follow-up story: it has to update each session in place, since the draft editor's delete-and-recreate would also delete each session's venue bookings and equipment.

DECIDED 2026-10-05: the important information (AC4) is: 'Date and time' (Starts at, Ends at), 'Expected attendance', 'Venue requirements' (Preferred room layout, The venue must have, Accessibility needs), and equipment requirements (changed on the Equipment tab). Everything else is ordinary, including Other accessibility notes and Anything else about the space (free text that venue matching does not read). A value changed and then changed back is not a change (TC12). As the form is edited, an amber alert 'These changes affect existing arrangements' reads 'You've changed: <list>. Any venue booking, equipment or registrations already arranged will be flagged for review, not changed.'

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: what gets flagged (AC5). Date and time flags the event's venue bookings (Pending or Approved, not yet ended), its equipment requests (Requested, Under review, Reserved or Partially fulfilled) and its registrations (if anyone is Registered or on the waiting list). Expected attendance and venue requirements flag only the venue bookings. Any attendance change counts, a decrease included: the coordinator judges whether the room still suits. Nothing is changed: the booking keeps its times and status, the equipment keeps its status, and no attendee is told anything.

RESOLVED 2026-10-05 (overlap check against open Jira stories): registration settings are not edited in this story. Configure Event Registration (SPM-64, Sprint 3) owns turning registration on or off, the capacity and the registration period, with its own rules (capacity within the booked room, reopening a closed period), so the Registration section was taken off this form. Flagging registrations when the capacity drops below the number registered, or registration is turned off, moved to SPM-64 as a new criterion (Jira updated). This story still flags registrations when the date or time changes, and refuses a start before registration closes, under Starts at: 'Registration closes after this start time. Change the registration period first.' (TC20).

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: who sees the flags, and where. The BPMN change path is 'Return event to Planning; notify organiser' -> 'Resume main flow at Planning', where the coordinator searches venues and submits booking and equipment requests again, so flags are the coordinator's: Venue Staff and Technical Support see a new or changed request, not a flag. This story shows only what a save flagged, to the coordinator who saved, on the edit page after saving: an amber alert 'Flagged for review', 'These were arranged for the event's earlier details and have not been changed.', one line per arrangement, e.g. 'Venue booking: Orchard Seminar Room (ORC-SEM) – the date or time changed', 'Equipment: 4K Portable Projector × 2 – the expected attendance changed', 'Registrations: 12 attendees – the date or time changed'. Reasons: 'the date or time changed', 'the expected attendance changed', 'the venue requirements changed', joined with '; '. Showing flags afterwards is Track Outstanding Arrangements (SPM-33) and Review Flagged Arrangements (SPM-68), so the event page itself is unchanged here. Flags are stored as VenueBooking.needsReview/reviewReason (as SPM-39 does), new EquipmentRequest.needsReview/reviewReason/flaggedAt columns (also needed by SPM-55), and a new Event.registrationReviewReason (also used by SPM-64).

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: reviewing and clearing flags is not part of this story. SPM-68 Review Flagged Arrangements (Sprint 3) gives the coordinator the list of flagged venue bookings and equipment with the reason, and keeping or replacing each one; it also makes a flagged arrangement block confirmation. When the coordinator replaces an arrangement, Venue Staff and Technical Support receive it as a new request.

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: reviewing flagged registrations is in Review Flagged Arrangements (SPM-68), extended in Jira: flagged registrations are listed with the number registered or waitlisted and why, the coordinator can mark them as reviewed (clearing the flag without changing any registration), and they do not prevent confirmation. SPM-32 and SPM-35 end when the change is applied, so neither covers it.

RESOLVED 2026-10-05 (overlap check): Release or Adjust Equipment Reservation (SPM-69) said a coordinator's change to a reserved equipment requirement flags the reservation for Technical Support, which contradicted the coordinator-only flags above. Reworded in Jira: the changed requirement goes back to Technical Support as Requested, showing what was already reserved, and is not flagged; SPM-75 reworded to match. Setting the requirement back to Requested is SPM-69's to build; this story only moves a Confirmed event back to Planning when its equipment changes.

DECIDED 2026-10-05: reverting a Confirmed event (AC6). It reverts when a saved change flags a venue booking or an equipment request, which are the arrangements confirmation depends on (SPM-34). Before saving, a dialog 'Move this event back to Planning?' reads '<title> is Confirmed. Saving these changes moves it back to Planning so it can be confirmed again.' with 'Keep editing' and 'Save and move to Planning'. The event moves to Planning, Confirmed at is cleared, and a status history entry is written: 'Event information changed: Date and time' (the list of changes).

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: equipment requirements on a Confirmed event (AC4, AC6). Adding, changing or removing an equipment requirement on the Equipment tab of a Confirmed event asks first, like the information form: 'Move this event back to Planning?' reading '<title> is Confirmed. Changing its equipment moves it back to Planning so it can be confirmed again.' with 'Cancel' and 'Continue' (the same buttons as the tab's 'Begin planning?' dialog, SPM-54). 'Remove' adds this notice to its own confirmation dialog instead of asking twice: 'It will also move from Confirmed back to Planning.' On Continue the event moves to Planning with history reasons 'Equipment requirement recorded / updated / removed', the tab shows an amber alert 'This event is no longer confirmed': 'Changing its equipment moved it back to Planning so it can be confirmed again.' (TC13).
DECIDED 2026-10-05: editing information on an Approved event does not begin planning (TC03, TC04). Only venue and equipment actions do (SPM-54).

RESOLVED 2026-10-05: no notifications are built in this story. Receive Event Notifications (SPM-53) already covers them: 'The Event Organiser is notified when a confirmed event is no longer confirmed', 'Relevant users are notified of important event changes' and 'Registered Attendees are notified of the new date and time when an event is rescheduled'. The BPMN's 'notify organiser (and attendees if date / time changes)' is met there. SPM-62's AC6 and SPM-32's description were reworded in Jira on 2026-10-05 to point to SPM-53.
